'''Autumn Kent''' is an American mathematician specializing in [[topology]] and [[geometry]]. She is a professor of [[mathematics]] and Vilas Associate at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin]].<ref name="wisc">{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/node/115|title=Staff Specializations {{!}} Department of Mathematics|website=www.math.wisc.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-05-01|archive-date=2021-03-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303221056/https://www.math.wisc.edu/node/115|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="vilas">{{cite web |url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/node/702 |title=Autumn Kent named as a Vilas Associate |access-date=2018-08-02 |website=www.math.wisc.edu |archive-date=2019-06-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607065949/https://www.math.wisc.edu/node/702 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailycardinal.com/article/2018/06/uw-madison-students-faculty-break-the-silence-about-campus-mental-health |title=UW-Madison students, faculty break the silence about campus mental health |last=Wallner |first=Grace |date=2018-06-12 |access-date=2018-08-14 |website=[[The Daily Cardinal]]}}</ref> She is a [[transgender woman]] and a promoter of [[trans rights]].<ref name="lamb">{{Cite news|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/roots-of-unity/q-a-with-autumn-kent/|title=Being a Trans Mathematician: A Q&A with Autumn Kent|last=Lamb|first=Evelyn|work=Scientific American Blog Network|access-date=2018-05-01|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://harvardgiim.org/wims/ |title=WIMS &ndash; Gender Inclusivity in Mathematics |website=Harvard Gender Inclusivity in Mathematics |access-date=2018-08-02 |date=2016-08-29 |archive-date=2019-03-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331181615/https://harvardgiim.org/wims/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="rewire">{{cite web|url=https://www.rewire.org/our-future/queer-scientists-stem-inclusivity/ |title=500 Queer Scientists Speak Up About STEM Inclusivity |website=rewire.org |date=2018-06-28 |last=Crowell |first=Rachel |access-date=2018-08-02}}</ref>

== Education ==
Kent received her B.A. from the [[University of North Carolina at Asheville]] in 1999.<ref name=cv/> Originally, she had planned to become a high-school English teacher, but she switched to mathematics, majoring in it and in literature.<ref name="brown">{{cite web|url=https://www.brown.edu/Administration/News_Bureau/2006-07/06-016.ps.html |title=New Physical Sciences Faculty 2006 |website=[[Brown University]] |access-date=2018-08-14 |date=2006-09-05}}</ref> She earned her Ph.D. under the advising of [[Cameron Gordon (mathematician)|Cameron McAllan Gordon]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 2006; her dissertation was entitled ''Geometry and Algebra of Hyperbolic 3-manifolds''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=116135}}</ref> After a four-year position as the Tamarkin Assistant Professor of Mathematics at [[Brown University]],<ref name="brown" /> she joined the faculty of University of Wisconsin–Madison in 2010. She became associate professor in 2016, and a full professor in 2020.<ref name=cv/><ref name="wisc"/>

==Career==
Kent has published over 20 papers in various journals, mostly regarding [[Low-dimensional topology|low dimensional topology]] and [[knot theory]]. Many of these were published under her former name, or [[deadname]], before she came out as transgender.<ref name="lamb"/><ref name="rewire"/><ref name=cv>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/~kent/cv.pdf|title=CV|last=Kent|first=Autumn|website=www.math.wisc.edu}}</ref>

Kent served on the Policy and Advocacy Committee for the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] from February 2019 through January 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Policy & Advocacy Committee |url=https://awm-math.org/about/committees/committee-rosters/ |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]}}</ref> In addition, she served on the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] Panel Discussion Promoting Inclusion in [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] at the 2019 [[Joint Mathematics Meeting]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2019/2217_otherorg |title= Activities of Other Organizations |website=[[Joint Mathematics Meetings]] |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/meetings/awm-jmm/awm-at-jmm-2019/ |title= AWM at JMM 2019 |website=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]] |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref> With [[Harrison Bray]], she organized the LG&TBQ+ conference at the [[University of Michigan]] to foster collaboration between [[LGBT|LGBTQ+]] mathematicians working in [[geometry]], [[topology]], and [[dynamical systems]] with funding from Kent's [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|NSF Career Award]].<ref name="nsfcar"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/~kent/LG&TBQ.about.html |title= LG&TBQ |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref> She gave the Spectra Lavender Lecture at the 2022 Joint Mathematics Meeting.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meetings (JMM) |first=Joint Mathematics |title=Joint Mathematics Meetings |url=https://www.jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2022/2268_invspeakers#driessche |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=Joint Mathematics Meetings |language=en}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1999, Kent won the Frank Gerth Dissertation Award.<ref name="brown"/> In 2014, she was awarded an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|NSF Career Award]] to study moduli of [[Riemann surface]]s.<ref name="nsfcar">{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1350075 |title=CAREER: Moduli of curves via topology, geometry, and arithmetic |website=[[National Science Foundation]] |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref>  In 2015 and 2016, she was a von Neumann Fellow at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Past von Neumann Fellow: Autumn Kent |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/autumn-kent |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date= |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]]|date=9 December 2019 }}</ref> She was named as a Vilas Associate at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] for 2018 and 2019.<ref name="vilas"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://research.wisc.edu/professorships-and-faculty-fellowships/vilas-associates/past-winners-vilas-associates/ |title=Past Winners Vilas Associates |website=[[University of Wisconsin]] |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref> In 2019, she received a [[Simons Foundation|Simons Fellowship]].<ref name="simons">{{cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2019/03/15/2019-simons-fellows-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-physics-announced/ |title=2019 Simons Fellows in Mathematics and Theoretical Physics Announced |website=[[Simons Foundation]] |access-date=2019-03-30|date=2019-03-15 }}</ref><ref name="badger">{{cite web|url=https://badgerherald.com/news/2019/03/26/three-uw-professors-receive-simons-fellowships-in-mathematics/ |title=Three UW professors receive Simons Fellowships in mathematics |website=[[The Badger Herald]] |date=26 March 2019 |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref><ref name="uw">{{cite web|url=https://news.wisc.edu/uw-madison-mathematicians-named-simons-fellows/ |title=UW–Madison mathematicians named Simons Fellows | website=[[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]  |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref><ref name="ams">{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=4977 |title=2019 Simons Fellows Announced  |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref>

She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2024 class of fellows.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2024|title=2024 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2023-11-09}}</ref>
